messages.text:
Summarize my conversation, action, decision and your (lead) conversation, action, decision including your subagents

You have to read the message conversation, timing and another related.
Then create claude artifact for explain and visualize this.
Let's delegate to agent for investigating this.

Started: five helper agents are summarizing all 10 days, then I build one Claude page that explains and visualizes it.
- Sources: every console thread, step and proposal with its time; my own session log (what I said, spawned, landed, decided); git history; incidents.
- Each helper takes 1-3 days and writes: your messages, actions and decisions; mine; and every agent spawned with its job and outcome.
- The page: a day-by-day timeline, who decided what, the agent tree, and the best-build path, with your words paraphrased and no personal data.
- Expected: about 30-45 minutes. I will post the link here.
What you need to do: nothing now.

The summary page is ready: https://claude.ai/artifact/<private-artifact> (private Claude page; only you can open it).
- What it covers: 30 Sep 17:05 to 9 Oct 12:57 UTC, day by day, in 3 lanes: You, Lead (me), Agents.
- Every day lists what went wrong, my own mistakes included (e.g. the retracted "Chrome 154" claim, the missed C-009 Done).
- Charts: activity per day, your 41 proposal decisions on a timeline, the best-build path v0 to g0.0l, agents by role.
- A table lists the 13 decisions of yours that shaped the study (worktrees, frozen site, swipe A/B, the g0 line, T-256...).

| Total | Count |
|---|---|
| Agents I started | 442 |
| Commits on main | 2,412 |
| Proposals (accepted / rejected) | 41 (36 / 2) |
| Incidents (tool or device problems) | 262 |

- How it was made: 5 helper agents each summarized 2 days from the threads, steps, proposals, my transcript and git; I checked their counts and fixed 2 errors (pronoun, who made the guard change).
- "Your messages" counts rows (chat lines, thread messages, step answers), so it is higher than the number of unique messages.
What you need to do: nothing; open the link, and comment on the page if a day is wrong or missing.
